subject: OpenModelHub request: community maintainer credits for Hack Week 2026
messages:
From: Aditi Rao <aditi@openmodelhub.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: maintainer / community credits for Hack Week 2026

Hi Ben,

Hope you're doing well — I'm Aditi, program lead at OpenModelHub. We're running Hack Week 2026 (May 6-8) and would love Redwood to sponsor credits for our community maintainers. The ask is straightforward:

- 50 maintainers
- 10,000 inference credits per maintainer (30-day window)
- Use cases: model evaluation, small demos, and CI inference for open-source tooling

We're happy to include Redwood as a community sponsor on the event page and run a short talk/demo slot (15 min) if you can help. I've attached a short brief with the breakdown and the event schedule.

Quick context: OpenModelHub is a non-profit that incubates model evaluation tooling and maintains a set of community models used by hundreds of student teams. Supporting maintainers helps preserve project health and surface Redwood to a cluster of ML students and OSS maintainers.

Can you let me know if this is something Redwood can approve or route to the right person? If helpful, happy to hop on a 15-minute call next week.

Thanks,
Aditi Rao
Program Lead, OpenModelHub
aditi@openmodelhub.org
(attachment: openmodelhub_ask_v3.pdf)

Thanks for the ping, Ben. A few quick questions before we commit:

- Can we get a short list / criteria of the "maintainers" who will receive credits (to avoid wide resale/fraud)?
- Are the credits time-limited (they mentioned 30 days)? Would prefer single-use promo codes linked to emails.
- What's the visibility / sponsorship level? Where does Redwood appear on site/announcements?

I'm provisionally supportive of a community allocation but would like a smaller pilot: 25 maintainers at 10k credits each, with a clear usage window and sponsor recognition. Monica — can you draft a one-page sponsor promo agreement and a simple distribution checklist? Rafael — any cost objections?

Laura

All — finance POV: we can approve a community pilot but recommend capping the dollar-equivalent. Proposed approval:

- Up to $3,000 USD equivalent promo (we'll translate into token/credits)
- Pilot distribution method: one-time promo codes tied to verified emails
- Require a short sponsor acknowledgement form (DocuSign) and a post-event short report (attendance + top usage metrics)

Monica — please attach the GL code and put together the internal cost tracking. Once we have the list of recipients and the signed sponsor acknowledgement, finance will issue the promotional credits.
